Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

acceptable adjective

also unacceptable, passable, all right (acceptable)

classical

Cic. Brut. 263 (Lewis & Short)

probābilis, probābile

declension

acceptable, commendable, good enough

First “likely, credible” (see probably); then, of people and things, worth approving, acceptable. What is unacceptable is often simply nōn probandum, or id nōn probō, I don’t accept that.

Other words

  • tolerābilis, tolerābile — bearable, tolerable, passable

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 104; Cic. Sen. 7

    What can be put up with; of an orator, passable (Cic. Brut. 178).

Examples

  • C. Licinius probābilis ōrātor, jam vērō etiam probātus

    Gaius Licinius, an acceptable speaker, and indeed an approved oneCic. Brut. 263 (Lewis & Short)

  • omnia autem brevia tolerābilia esse dēbent, etiamsī magna sunt

    but everything short ought to be bearable, even if it is greatCic. Amic. 104

See also suitable.
